subject: Aurora account renewal - request for terms exception
messages:
From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@aurorasoft.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: julia.park@aurorasoft.com, legal@aurorasoft.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora renewal — asking for flexibility

Rafael,

We're coming up on our renewal and I'm having a candid internal conversation with our CFO. Due to a re-prioritization of product spend across Q3, AuroraSoft needs to reduce TCO for the next 12 months. We're evaluating a short list of vendors and I want Redwood to remain on the table — but we need a more favorable package.

What would be possible on your side for the following: 1) a one-year price reduction (~25% target), 2) an SLA credit scheme in the event of regressions to match our risk posture, and 3) the option to reset the contract term to 12 months with a mid-year review? If those items aren't available, we'll likely move the workload to a commodity provider.

I've attached a brief sketch of our requirements (Aurora_Renewal_Req.pdf).

Can you nominate the right person to take this to your leadership? We need clarity by EOD next Friday.

Thanks,
Marcus Hale
VP, Infrastructure
AuroraSoft

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: sales-ops@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Aurora renewal — asking for flexibility (needs exec approval)

Laura / Marissa,

Forwarding a renewal escalation from Aurora (DL-2026-0791). They are asking for ~25% off, SLA credits, and a 12-month term reset. Account health: multi-year customer, $1.1M ARR, low usage growth but high strategic importance — reference customer for financial services use case. Risk of churn is real if we don't bridge.

Proposal I think we should consider for approval (short list):
- One-time structure: 15% list discount year 1 + $50,000 one-time credit applied at renewal
- SLA: formal addendum guaranteeing 99.9% uptime for core inference endpoints for 12 months; make credit formula symmetrical and capped
- Term: 24-month commitment with the first 12 months priced as above (i.e., term reset coupled with a minimum spend floor to protect unit economics)

Why this: hits customer ask for near-term relief while preserving multi-quarter revenue and protecting margin via a commit. Finance impact ~ -$115k in year-1 net revenue vs list if accepted; but reduces churn risk and preserves cross-sell.

Attached a short save-sheet and suggested SLA language. Can you confirm if you can sign off on this authority or if this needs next-level exec? If approved, I will prepare a tracked proposal and loop Legal for the addendum. They need an answer by next Friday (2027-06-11).

Attachments: Aurora_Save_Term_Sheet.pdf

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Strategic
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: finance-approvals@redwood.com, legal-approvals@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Aurora renewal — asking for flexibility (needs exec approval)

Rafael — good summary. I approve a constrained concession with conditions.

Decision (authorized):
- Discount: approve up to 15% off list for year 1 only.
- Credit: one-time $50,000 credit to be applied at renewal execution (not refundable).
- SLA: approve 99.9% uptime addendum for core inference endpoints for 12 months; any credits triggered must be capped at the one-time $50k and require documented postmortem and remediation plan.
- Term & commitment: require a 24-month contract term with a minimum annual spend floor (to be defined by Finance) and an auto-renew clause; if customer does not meet floors, revert to standard pricing at the next renewal.

Conditions:
1) Finance must confirm the minimum spend floor and sign off on the margin impact (assigned: @finance-approvals).
2) Legal to draft a short SLA addendum and an amendment reflecting the one-time credit (assigned: @legal-approvals).
3) Sales Ops to record the concession in the deal record and limit to this single-year exception.

Rafael — proceed to prepare a formal term sheet for Aurora, include the margin impact and the proposed commit language, and loop legal/finance. Mark the deal with ID DL-2026-0791 and tag as a "one-time concession".

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — MidMarket
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@aurorasoft.com>
Cc: julia.park@aurorasoft.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aurora renewal — asking for flexibility

Marcus — thanks for the candid note and for giving us time to review. We had an expedited internal review and can offer the following limited, conditional package to preserve AuroraSoft on Redwood: 

1) Commercial: 15% off list pricing for year 1 (applied at signature) + a one-time credit of $50,000 applied to the renewal invoice.
2) SLA: a 12-month SLA addendum guaranteeing 99.9% uptime for the core inference endpoints. Any SLA credits would be applied per the addendum and are capped at the $50k one-time credit; credits require documented incident analysis and remediation commitments.
3) Term: require a 24-month contract term with a minimum annual spend floor; the first 12 months will carry the concession pricing above. If minimum floors are not met, we will revert to standard pricing at the next renewal.

Attached: Proposed_SLA_Addendum.docx; Aurora_Save_Term_Sheet.pdf (term sheet showing impact and payment schedule).

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute call early next week so I can walk through the small set of legal language and the commit floor? If you are agreeable in principle, I will initiate the amendment paperwork and route it to Legal + Finance.

If you'd like the contract to reflect a one-year priced discount rather than a true 12-month term reset, let me know — we can model both but my recommendation is the commit to preserve revenue predictability.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Strategic
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: Proposed_SLA_Addendum.docx (SLA addendum draft), Aurora_Save_Term_Sheet.pdf (commercial impact & sample clause)
